subject: LLM data governance and opt-out: request for operational proofs
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@blueharbor.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-05-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: LLM data governance and opt-out: request for operational proofs

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, Legal and InfoSec asked me to consolidate a short list of operational proofs we need to sign off on before we can finalize a contract amendment. High-level asks: 

- A firm "no-training" (no model improvement) commitment for tenant data, ideally contractually scoped and operationalized.
- Current subprocessor inventory + attestation that BlueHarbor data will not be used to improve models.
- KMS/key residency options and any onshore-only support (we're US-based but have EU patients).
- Evidence of deletion/retention flows and audit logs for inquiries.

Can you confirm which items Redwood can provide as artifacts vs. language we need in the SOW/DPA? If you can point us to a single folder or post a short attestation XLS, that would help Legal move faster.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Tom Ellis
Sr. Procurement Manager, BlueHarbor Health
procurement@blueharbor.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: LLM data governance and opt-out: request for operational proofs

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can operationalize a contractual no-training commitment and provide the operational artifacts you're asking for. I'll outline next steps below and loop in Legal and Ops for delivery timelines.

High-level plan / owners:
- Legal redline (David) — draft amendment language (no-training + subprocessor attestation requirement). Target: first pass in 3 business days.
- Ops evidence (Neha) — provide subprocessor inventory XLS + an ops runbook describing retention, deletion, KV-prefix caching behavior, and audit log exports. Target: artifacts posted to a secure folder within 5 business days.
- KMS/residency (Kimberly) — list of supported KMS regions and options for onshore key escrow or customer-managed keys.

We will also include an operational attestation statement that you can attach to the DPA — a short signed PDF confirming Redwood will not surface BlueHarbor tenant data for model improvement and will treat prompts/responses as customer content per the amendment.

Next steps for you: confirm any mandatory phrasing (e.g., "no derivatives" vs "no training") or whether your security team requires an onshore-only KMS for US data. If you prefer, we can set a focused 30-min call Wednesday to walk through the artifacts.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-06T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LLM data governance and opt-out: request for operational proofs

Sean / Tom — quick legal note on scope and artifacts. Thanks for the outline Sean; below is the language and evidence matrix I'd like to land on before we send a formal amendment.

1) Contract language (short form) — propose an amendment clause:
   "Redwood will not use Customer Content (including prompts, uploads, and model outputs) to train, finetune, or otherwise improve any models used in the Redwood service for the duration of the agreement, except where Customer gives explicit, written consent."

   - Clarify: "no derivatives" is broader (it can affect service features). We should make the clause explicitly about model improvement/training to avoid blocking product telemetry that doesn't impact model weights.

2) Subprocessor attestations — we will provide:
   - Current subprocessor inventory (names + roles)
   - Signed attestation (ops team) that BlueHarbor tenant data is excluded from model training pipelines.

3) Evidence items (what Ops will provide):
   - Subprocessor_Attestation.xlsx (inventory + signed column)
   - Ops_Runbook_NoTrain.pdf (runbook describing QA gates, KV cache policies, and deletion flows)
   - Audit log excerpt showing retention and access controls (redacted)

4) KMS/residency — Kimberly, please confirm whether we can offer US-only CMK or onshore key escrow for BlueHarbor. If not feasible, we should document the compensating controls.

Tom: once Ops posts the artifacts I'll review and circulate a short amendment and an attestation PDF you can attach to your procurement packet. If BlueHarbor Legal wants additional wording (e.g., indemnity tied to a breach of the no-train commitment), flag that now so we can triage.

Tom / Sean / David — attaching the artifacts we discussed. See attachments (stubs) below and a short summary of what each contains. I uploaded full redacted artifacts to the secure folder and shared the link with your procurement address.

Attachments (included):
- Subprocessor_Attestation.xlsx (attachment stub) — inventory of subprocessors, role, jurisdiction, and an ops-signed attestation column confirming BlueHarbor tenant data is excluded from model training pipelines.
- Ops_Runbook_NoTrain.pdf (attachment stub) — describes the operational flow: inbound request handling, ephemeral KV cache policy, retention and deletion, and the audit-log export process.

Quick ops clarifications:
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can host CMKs in US regions. We also offer an onshore key-escrow option for enterprise customers; Kimberly will follow up with availability and pricing.
- Audit logs: we can provide redacted access logs and a sample lineage export. Full log export is available via SFTP/API for eDiscovery requests.
- Attestation: we will produce a signed attestation PDF that Legal can attach to an amended DPA.

Links: secure evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A3_example_evidence
